sections.h2: Who bills property tax for a Greensboro home?
sections.html:
Guilford County, not the City of Greensboro, sends the bill, and the city levy rides on the same statement. The Guilford County Tax Department keeps counters at 400 W. Market St. in Greensboro and 325 E. Russell Ave. in High Point, both staffed 8 a.m. to 5 p.m. Monday through Friday.

Dial 336-641-4814 about values and appeals. The county's FAQ names 336-641-3363 for anyone who wants to arrange paying a balance in full before the delinquent date. Greensboro sets its own levy, and the county's table shows it on a separate line.

Lenders that escrow ask the county for your bill each summer and mail you a notice. Under North Carolina law, getting the tax paid stays the owner's job, so if the lender named on that notice is not yours, pass it to the correct servicer.

sections.h2: What property tax rates apply inside Greensboro?
sections.html:
The county's 2026-2027 rate page prints a countywide rate of 0.78950 and a City of Greensboro rate of 0.79850, for a total of 1.58800 under rate code 01. The county explains that its rates are fractions of $1 for each $100 of value.

A $30 vehicle fee also applies in Greensboro, and the county says it is neither discounted nor penalized.

sections.h2: How did Senate Bill 889 change Greensboro property tax bills?
sections.html:
It froze the use of the 2026 reappraisal values for one year, so bills for the fiscal year that began July 1, 2026 rest on the older values. The City of Greensboro says the moratorium applies to the county's revaluation process and does not stop local governments from changing their rates.

  • Greensboro adopted its fiscal year 2026-27 budget on June 16, with a total city rate of 79.85 cents.
  • The city describes that as a 12.6-cent adjustment on current property values, not on the new reappraisal values.
  • The county says the updated values are paused until January 1, 2027, and are expected to feed the budget year that begins July 1, 2027.

The practical result: your new notice of value does not set this year's bill. It still matters, because if the value is wrong, the appeal clock runs on it, and an appeal that stays open now is considered for the 2027 tax year.

sections.h2: When are Greensboro property taxes due, and how can I pay?
sections.html:
The due date is September 1, and a bill stays free of interest through January 5 (G.S. 105-360). The county's FAQ then charges 2% for the first month and adds 0.75% on the first of every month that follows.

  • Discount: Guilford County and Greensboro give 1.0% off for payment before September 1, per the county rate page.
  • Online, or by phone at (336) 203-7795: 1.85% processing charge and a $2 transaction fee.
  • At a tax office counter: cash and checks are free, while a card carries 2.35% and $2.
  • Mail: Guilford County Tax Department, P.O. Box 70939, Charlotte, NC 28272-0939.

The USPS postmark fixes the date of a mailed payment, and proving it was on time falls to the taxpayer. The county says it phones about payment only when a bill is delinquent, and gift cards are never accepted.

sections.h2: What is the process for appealing a Greensboro value?
sections.html:
Send it to the Guilford County Tax Department. The county's appeals page accepts 2026 filings through December 31, 2026, and 2027 filings through May 17, 2027, when the online portal opens January 1, 2027.

An owner who already appealed the reappraisal value does not need to refile, because that appeal carries into tax year 2027. The deadline originally published was May 15, 2026, at 5 p.m.

For a paper form, the county advises handing it to a postal clerk for a hand-cancelled postmark, since a mailbox drop can be stamped the next day with no proof. Anything postmarked after May 17 is rejected. Before the portal opens, a form can be requested at taxreval@guilfordcountync.gov.

The board hears whatever staff cannot settle, and the next stop is the state Property Tax Commission, with notice due 30 days after the board mails its decision (G.S. 105-290). Personal property is a separate track with its own 30-day window from the notice date.

sections.h2: What tax relief can Greensboro homeowners apply for?
sections.html:
Greensboro homeowners may use any of three state programs, with a June 1 filing deadline each year. Mail applications to Guilford County Tax Department, PO Box 3138, Greensboro, NC 27402, or carry them to either tax office.

  • Elderly or disabled exclusion: $25,000 or half the value, whichever is more, off the home of a qualifying 65-plus or disabled owner whose gross income stays under $38,800 on the county's page. One application is enough.
  • Circuit breaker: the tax is held to 4% or 5% of income, using the printed caps of $38,800 and $58,200, after five years of owning and living in the home. It is renewed annually.
  • Disabled veteran exclusion: the first $45,000 of value, with no age or income test, applied for once.

Only one program per owner is allowed. The county will still review a late application if it arrives at least one week before the last equalization board meeting in December. Questions go to 336-641-3320 or 336-641-7911. A circuit breaker owner who sells owes the last three years of deferred tax, with interest, on the sale date.

sections.h2: What happens when Greensboro property tax goes unpaid before a sale?
sections.html:
Interest starts, collection begins at once, and the tax remains a lien on the parcel. The county's FAQ lists wage and bank garnishment, levies on personal property, attachment of state refunds and lottery winnings, and foreclosure on real estate.

Under G.S. 105-355 the lien dates from the listing date and includes penalties and costs. A foreclosure action under G.S. 105-374 ends at a courthouse-door auction, and redemption before confirmation requires paying taxes, interest, penalties and costs. The county says it holds no tax lien sales.

Before listing, ask the tax department for the figures on the current bill. A deferred balance under a relief program is a separate item, so ask for it by name.

sections.h2: How big is Greensboro and who lives in its homes?
sections.html:
QuickFacts shows Greensboro at 308,667 people in 2025, compared with 299,035 in the 2020 Census and 269,666 in 2010. The city occupies about 130 square miles of land, which works out to about 2,308 people for each.

  • Households: 123,984, averaging 2.29 people (2020 to 2024).
  • Owner-occupied homes: 50.5%.
  • Value of the typical owner's home: $244,800.
  • Typical gross rent: $1,172.
  • Typical household income: $61,515.
  • Average commute: 21.7 minutes.
  • Adults with a bachelor's degree or more: 41.0%.

Owners and renters are nearly even, so a Greensboro sale often has a landlord on one side. Typical monthly owner costs with a mortgage are $1,447, which gives a baseline to hold against your own tax line.

faqs.q: Which government mails the Greensboro tax statement?
faqs.a: Guilford County. Its tax department bills the county and city levies together from counters at 400 W. Market St., Greensboro, and 325 E. Russell Ave., High Point.

faqs.q: What total rate does a city parcel carry?
faqs.a: Rate code 01 totals 1.58800 in the county's 2026-2027 table, made of 0.78950 countywide plus 0.79850 for Greensboro. Historic and downtown districts add more.
Yes. Guilford County and Greensboro each allow a 1.0% discount for paying before September 1, according to the rate page.

faqs.q: Is an appeal still possible after the moratorium?
faqs.a: Yes. Guilford accepts 2026 appeals through December 31, 2026, and 2027 appeals through May 17, 2027, with its online portal starting January 1, 2027. Earlier appeals stay active.

faqs.q: Does Guilford County auction tax liens to investors?
faqs.a: No. The tax department says it conducts no tax lien sales, though it enforces collection with garnishment and real estate foreclosure.
